Glider 1.0.2

A new Activity window, a fresh look, and crash reports to find and fix problems faster.

  • Activity: see your uploads, and those of Glider on your other devices, in one list. Each file says whether it was added, replaced, renamed, or brought in or removed by two-way sync. Name this Mac in Settings so your other devices know where a file came from.
  • A new app icon, and icons in the menu-bar menu. The menu-bar bird now changes while files upload.
  • Finder: right-click › Quick Actions › Upload with Glider, from a new Finder extension. If it is turned off in Settings, Glider says so.
  • Glider Lite, a lighter edition for the Mac App Store, copies files to Dropbox instead of moving them.
  • Glider now sends crash reports and anonymous usage statistics through Google Firebase. They never include your files, file names, Dropbox paths or sign-in, and are not used for ads or tracking. Details in the privacy policy.

Glider 1.0.1

The first release of Glider: drop files and they glide into your Dropbox.

  • Drop files on the Dock icon, the menu-bar bird or the drop zone that appears while you drag, or right-click › Services › Upload with Glider.
  • A Glider folder per account, kept in two-way sync with Dropbox › Apps › GliderApp.
  • Several Dropbox accounts, large files in resumable pieces, and a choice of copy or move.
